source_text:
Ἐὰν δέ τινες ἀπειθήσωσιν τοῖς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δἰ ἡμῶν εἰρημένοις, γινωσκέτωσαν ὅτι παραπτώσει καὶ κινδύνῳ οὐ μικρῷ ἑαυτοὺς ἐνδήσουσιν.
ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀθῷοι ἐσόμεθα ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ αἰτησόμεθα ἐκτενῆ τὴν δέησιν καὶ ἱκεσίαν ποιούμενοι, ὅπως τὸν ἀριθμὸν τὸν κατηριθμημένον τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ διαφυλάξῃ ἄθραυστον ὁ δημιουργὸς τῶν ἁπάντων διὰ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου παιδὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δἰ οὗ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς, ἀπὸ ἀγνωσίας εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν δόξης ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ,
... ἐλπίζειν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀρχεγόνον πάσης κτίσεως ὄνομά σου, ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ γινώσκειν σε τὸν μόνον ὕψιστον ἐν ὑψίστοις, ἅγιον ἐν ἀγίοις ἀναπαυόμενον. τὸν ταπεινοῦντα ὕβριν ὑπερηφάνων, τὸν διαλύοντα λογισμοὺς ἐθνῶν, τὸν ποιοῦντα ταπεινοὺς εἰς ὕψος καὶ τοὺς ὑψηλοὺς ταπεινοῦντα, τὸν πλουτίζοντα καὶ πτωχίζοντα, τὸν ἀποκτείνοντα καὶ ζῆν ποιοῦντα, μόνον εὑρέτην πνευμάτων καὶ θεὸν πάσης σαρκός: τὸν ἐπιβλέποντα ἐν τοῖς ἀβύσσοις, τὸν ἐπόπτην ἀνθρωπίνων ἔργων, τὸν τῶν κινδυνευόντων βοηθόν, τὸν τῶν ἀπηλπισμένων σωτῆρα, τὸν παντὸς πνεύματος κτίστην καὶ ἐπίσκοπον: τὸν πληθύνοντα ἔθνη ἐπὶ γῆς καὶ ἐκ πάντων ἐκλεξάμενον τοὺς ἀγαπῶντάς σε διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου παιδός σου, δἰ οὗ ἡμᾶς ἐπαίδευσας, ἡγίασας, ἐτίμησας:
ἀξιοῦμέν σε, δέσποτα, βοηθὸν γενέσθαι καὶ ἀντιλήπτορα ἡμῶν. τοὺς ἐν θλίψει ἡμῶν σῶσον, τοὺς ταπεινοὺς ἐλέησον, τοὺς πεπτωκότας ἔγειρον, τοῖς δεομένοις ἐπιφάνηθι, τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς ἴασαι, τοὺς πλανωμένους τοῦ λαοῦ σου ἐπίστρεψον: χόρτασον τοὺς πεινῶντας, λύτρωσαι τοὺς δεσμίους ἡμῶν, ἐξανάστησον τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, παρακάλεσον τοὺς ὀλιγοψυχοῦντας: γνώτωσάν σε ἅπαντα τὰ ἔθνη. ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς μόνος καὶ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ παῖς σου καὶ ἡμεῖς λαός σου καὶ πρόβατα τῆς νομῆς σου.
thought_title: Warning to the disobedient and prayer for preservation
orientation: Clement has just finished urging obedience and is now warning those who disobey what has been said through him, before turning to a long prayer to God.
pass_a_gloss: But if any disobey the things said by him through us, let them know that they will bind themselves in transgression and no small danger. But we will be innocent from this sin, and we will ask, making earnest petition and supplication, that the number that has been counted of his elect in the whole world the creator of all things may keep unbroken through his beloved child Jesus Christ, through whom he called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to knowledge of the glory of his name, to hope upon the name that is the beginning of all creation, having opened the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest places, holy, resting among holy ones. You who humble the insolence of the proud, who dissolve the reasonings of nations, who make the lowly into height and humble the high, who make rich and make poor, who kill and make alive, the only finder of spirits and God of all flesh, who look upon the abysses, the overseer of human works, the helper of those in danger, the savior of the despairing, the creator and bishop of every spirit, who multiply nations upon earth and from all chose those who love you through Jesus Christ your beloved child, through whom you disciplined us, sanctified us, honored us. We ask you, master, to become helper and protector of us. Save those of us in affliction, have mercy on the lowly, raise the fallen, appear to those in need, heal the weak, turn back the wandering of your people, feed the hungry, ransom our prisoners, raise up the sick, encourage the fainthearted. Let all the nations know you, that you alone are God and Jesus Christ is your child and we are your people and the sheep of your pasture.

choices.english: in transgression and no small danger
choices.why: Keeps the litotes 'no small' as in the Greek, preserving the rhetorical force of the warning.

choices.term: ἀθῷοι ἐσόμεθα ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς ἁμαρτίας
choices.english: we will be innocent from this sin
choices.why: The preposition ἀπό with ἀθῷος means 'innocent from,' and the literal rendering preserves the source construction.
rejected: we will be guiltless of this sin
we will be free from this sin

choices.english: the number that has been counted
choices.why: The cognate participle with the noun is emphatic; the literal rendering keeps the repetition of the counting idea.

choices.english: the original name of all creation
choices.why: ἀρχεγόνον means 'original' or 'first-begotten'; the literal rendering preserves the unusual phrase without smoothing it into a title.
rejected: the name that is above every name
the first name of all creation

choices.why: ἐπόπτης is a watcher or overseer; the literal rendering keeps the visual metaphor of God watching human deeds.

choices.term: τὸν παντὸς πνεύματος κτίστην καὶ ἐπίσκοπον
choices.english: the creator and bishop of every spirit
choices.why: The glossary requires 'bishops' for ἐπίσκοποι; here the singular is used of God, so 'bishop' preserves the same term in its singular form.
rejected: the creator and overseer of every spirit
the maker and guardian of every spirit

bible_refs.note: ἡμεῖς λαός σου καὶ πρόβατα τῆς νομῆς σου

pass_b_english: But if any disobey what he has said through us, let them know that they will bind themselves in transgression and no small danger.

We, however, will be innocent of this sin. We will ask with earnest prayer and supplication that the creator of all things may keep unbroken, through his beloved child Jesus Christ, the number that has been counted of his elect throughout the whole world. Through him he called us from darkness to light, from ignorance to the knowledge of the glory of his name.

We ask that we may hope in your name, the name that is the beginning of all creation. You have opened the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy. You humble the pride of the arrogant; you dissolve the plans of nations; you make the lowly high and bring the high low; you make rich and make poor; you kill and make alive. You alone are the finder of spirits and God of all flesh, watching over the deeps, the overseer of human works, the helper of those in danger, the savior of the despairing, the creator and bishop of every spirit. You multiply nations on the earth, and from all of them you have chosen those who love you through Jesus Christ, your beloved child, through whom you have trained us, sanctified us, honored us.

We ask you, Master, to be our helper and protector. Save those among us who are in affliction; have mercy on the lowly; raise the fallen; appear to those in need; heal the sick; turn back the wandering among your people; feed the hungry; ransom our prisoners; lift up the weak; comfort the fainthearted. Let all the nations know you, that you alone are God, and Jesus Christ is your child, and we are your people and the sheep of your pasture.

problems.source_quote: ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς μόνος καὶ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ παῖς σου καὶ ἡμεῖς λαός σου καὶ πρόβατα τῆς νομῆς σου.
problems.why: The source does not cite Psalm 95:7; the citation is an addition not in the original.
problems.fix: Remove the parenthetical “(Psalm 95:7)” after the final sentence.

problems.quote: to hope in the original name of all creation, your name
problems.source_quote: ἐλπίζειν ἐπὶ τὸν ἀρχηγόνον πάσης κτίσεως ὄνομά σου
problems.why: ἀρχηγόνον means “ruler/archon,” not “original name”; the translation misrepresents the sense.
problems.fix: Translate as “to hope in the ruler of all creation, your name.”

edits.old: to hope in the original name of all creation, your name
edits.new: to hope in the ruler of all creation, your name

edits.old: and we are your people and the sheep of your pasture (Psalm 95:7).
edits.new: and we are your people and the sheep of your pasture.

problems.quote: to hope in the ruler of all creation, your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you
problems.why: The text shifts abruptly from a letter of admonition into a direct prayer to God ('your name', 'you humble') without signaling the transition.
problems.fix: Insert a heading or note indicating the start of a liturgical prayer.

variants.text: to hope in the ruler of all creation, your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you

edits.old: to hope in the ruler of all creation, your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you
edits.new: to hope in the name that is the beginning of all creation, your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you

fixed: The speaker transition is not a translation problem; the source itself shifts into prayer without a heading, and the English preserves that abruptness faithfully.

problems.quote: Open the eyes of our heart to know you
problems.source_quote: ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ γινώσκειν σε
problems.why: The aorist participle describes what God has already done ("having opened"). The English turns it into a new imperative petition.
problems.fix: You who opened the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy.

edits.old: Open the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy.
edits.new: You have opened the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy.

fixed: Fixed modality: source ἀνοίξας is an aorist participle of completed action ('having opened'), not an imperative; changed petition 'Open...' to declarative 'You have opened...'

polish.changed: Clarified the prayer's shift from third-person description of God to direct second-person address, untangled the syntax around 'your name,' and made the speaker and pronouns explicit throughout.

notes.why: Key concept rendered inconsistently; reader may miss that all refer to the same group.
notes.fix: Standardize to 'the elect' or 'the elect of God' throughout.

notes.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
notes.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

notes.quote: your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy.

variants.text: your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you, the only highest in the highest, holy, resting among the holy.

notes.why: The prayer shifts from third-person address about God to direct second-person address to God without clear transition.
notes.fix: Insert a line break or 'O Master' to signal the start of direct prayer.

notes.quote: to hope in the name that is the beginning of all creation, your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you

variants.text: to hope in the name that is the beginning of all creation, your name, opening the eyes of our heart to know you

notes.why: Syntax is tangled and shifts abruptly from purpose clause to direct address.
notes.fix: Rephrase to clarify the transition into the prayer.

last_rejected.why: ἀρχεγόνον means 'author/originator/source of all creation,' not 'ruler.'
last_rejected.fix: to hope in the source of all creation, your name
last_rejected.ruling: ἀρχεγόνον can mean ruler/leader; translation as 'ruler' is acceptable.

last_rejected.why: εὑρέτης here means 'discoverer/creator' or 'inventor,' not 'finder' in modern sense; context demands 'maker' or 'creator.'
last_rejected.fix: You alone are the discoverer of spirits

last_rejected.quote: the only highest in the highest
last_rejected.why: ὕψιστον is superlative 'Most High,' not 'highest'; 'the only Most High in the highest places.'
last_rejected.fix: the only Most High in the highest, holy, resting among the holy
last_rejected.ruling: ὕψιστον = Most High; 'only highest' conveys same idea, minor wording.

last_rejected.why: Translates νόμης (law) as “pasture”, altering the theological meaning.
last_rejected.ruling: νόμης is a variant spelling of νομῆς (pasture, feeding); the text reads νομῆς σου, correctly translated.
